company.name: Micron Technology, Inc.
company.primary_assets: Wafer Fab Production Equipment, Buildings (Fabs), Construction in Progress, Software, Finance Lease ROU Assets
company.coverage_note: Micron财年为截至8月31日最近周四的52/53周期间；FY2022为2021-09-03至2022-09-01（52周），签署日期2022-10-07（HTML第3697行）。FY2022是存储周期顶部年：收入$30,758M（+11% YoY）、毛利率45%、净利润$8,687M，与FY2023底部年（收入$15,540M、净亏$5,833M）形成天然对照。注意Q4 FY2022行业环境急剧恶化（收入环比-23%），下行在财年末已开始。

financial_highlights.impairment_note: FY2022 'Restructure and asset impairments' 合计$48M（利润表L2591；注释L3372），主要为Q1 FY2022出售Lehi工厂确认的$23M处置损失（L2783-2784）——属FY2021 $435M Lehi减值周期的收尾，非新增技术退出减值。FY2022无商誉减值（定性测试通过，L2429-2432）、无存货NRV减记（全文未披露任何本期减记金额，仅披露敏感性：ASP变动5%→NRV变动约$337M，L2491-2493）。
financial_highlights.inventory_writedown_note: NA - FY2022未披露任何存货NRV减记金额（对比FY2023的$1,831M）；存货NRV估计为审计师关键审计事项（L3578-3605），截至2022-09-01产成品+在产品存货约$5.9B，ASP敏感性5%≈$337M（L2491-2493）。
financial_highlights.facility_underutilization_note: NA - FY2022未披露产能闲置成本（对比FY2023的$382M）；FY2021/FY2020分别有MTU闲置成本$335M/$557M（L2136-2138），随Lehi出售而终止。FY2022年末公司仅预告Q1 FY2023将'selectively reducing facility utilization'（L2127-2129）。
financial_highlights.finance_lease_note: 融资活动现金流-融资租赁：FY2022 $103M（另经营活动利息$23M）。融资租赁ROU资产$904M计入PP&E（L2895）；另有已签约未起租融资租赁义务$212M（14年加权期限，L2896-2899）。

accounting_policy.production_equipment_useful_life_years: 7 (anchor; FY2022 10-K披露口径为'5 to 7 years for equipment'，FY2023 10-K细化为'7 years for production equipment, up to 7 years for other equipment'——披露措辞细化而非估计变更，两年均未披露任何年限调整)
accounting_policy.assets_held_for_sale: lower of estimated fair value or carrying value; included in current assets
accounting_policy.useful_life_assessment_basis: periodically assessed based on technology node transitions, capital spending, and equipment re-use rates
accounting_policy.long_lived_asset_impairment_test: undiscounted expected future cash flows vs carrying value; impairment = excess of carrying value over estimated fair value
accounting_policy.change_in_estimate_method: NA - FY2022未披露任何折旧年限变更（延长或缩短）；全文检索'prospectively'/'change in estimate'正文零命中（已核实）。与FY2023确认版一致：连续两年无年限调整，政策中性。
accounting_policy.policy_risk_note: FY2022披露口径为设备5-7年直线折旧（建筑物10-30年、软件3-5年），上限7年与FY2023锚点一致。公司在关键会计估计中同样将年限与'技术节点迁移、资本开支、设备复用率'挂钩（L2505-2508）。FY2022为盈利顶部年，7年折旧假设在高利用率下显得'无害'，但Q4行业急剧恶化已在财年末发生（收入环比-23%），而年限未做任何调整——与FY2023底部年同样无调整互为印证：Micron的估计裁量在周期两端均呈'不作为'特征。跨年口径注意：FY2022的'5 to 7 years for equipment'与FY2023的'7 years for production equipment'是披露细化（上限一致），不构成年限变更。

risk_signals.source: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements - Significant Accounting Policies - Property, Plant, and Equipment
risk_signals.keyword_matched: useful lives of generally ... 5 to 7 years for equipment
risk_signals.text_excerpt: Property, plant, and equipment is stated at cost and depreciated using the straight-line method over estimated useful lives of generally 10 to 30 years for buildings, 5 to 7 years for equipment, and 3 to 5 years for software.
risk_signals.page_location: Notes - Significant Accounting Policies - Property, Plant, and Equipment (HTML lines 2717-2719)
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: Official depreciation schedule: fab equipment is depreciated straight-line over 5-7 years (7-year upper bound anchors D1, consistent with FY2023's refined wording '7 years for production equipment'). Against a DRAM/NAND node cadence of ~1-2 years per generation (1x/1y/1z/1-alpha in production, 1-beta ramping 2023), the 7-year life spans 3-5 node generations. Equipment gross is $61,354M - the dominant asset class - driving $7.03B of FY2022 depreciation.
evidence_chain: Official equipment life: 5-7 years straight-line (lines 2717-2719); upper bound 7 years consistent with FY2023 anchor
Equipment gross: $61,354M of $81,331M total PP&E gross (line 2870); FY2022 depreciation $7.03B
Node cadence: 2022 sales on 1x/1y/1z/1-alpha nodes while 1-beta on track to ramp in 2023 (lines 230-232); 232-layer NAND announced (line 643)
EUV lithography planned on the DRAM node after 1-beta (lines 640-641) - each such transition can strand or devalue pre-EUV tools
Result: 7-year life assumes multi-node tool reuse; depreciation is back-loaded relative to economic value loss if node turnover accelerates

risk_signals.source: MD&A - Critical Accounting Estimates - Property, Plant, and Equipment
risk_signals.keyword_matched: useful lives ... based on technology node transitions
risk_signals.text_excerpt: We periodically assess the estimated useful lives of our property, plant, and equipment based on technology node transitions, capital spending, and equipment re-use rates. We also review the carrying value of property, plant, and equipment for impairment when events and circumstances indicate that the carrying value of an asset or group of assets may not be recoverable from the estimated future cash flows expected to result from its use and/or disposition.
risk_signals.page_location: Item 7. MD&A - Critical Accounting Estimates (HTML lines 2505-2512)
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: Management itself names 'technology node transitions' as a primary driver of useful-life estimates - identical wording to the FY2023 filing, confirming cross-year policy continuity. Despite Q4 FY2022's sharp industry deterioration and the 1-beta/EUV transition underway, NO useful-life revision was made in FY2022, leaving the 7-year assumption unchanged at the cycle peak - the same 'no action' stance later maintained through the FY2023 trough.
evidence_chain: Company admits useful lives are a critical estimate driven by node transitions and re-use rates (lines 2505-2508)
FY2022: Q4 revenue -23% QoQ, gross margin 47%->39% (lines 2102-2124), yet no life revision disclosed
Undiscounted-cash-flow recoverability test is a weak backstop at asset-group level
Estimate discretion is inactive at BOTH cycle peak (FY2022) and trough (FY2023) - depreciation lacks cycle adaptivity
Result: depreciation schedule embeds a normal-utilization, stable-node assumption

risk_signals.source: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements - Property, Plant, and Equipment
risk_signals.text_excerpt: As of 2022 2021 Land $ 280 $ 280 Buildings 16,676 14,776 Equipment (1) 61,354 51,902 Construction in progress (2) 1,897 1,517 Software 1,124 987 81,331 69,462 Accumulated depreciation ( 42,782 ) ( 36,249 ) $ 38,549 $ 33,213 (1) Includes costs related to equipment not placed into service of $ 3.35 billion as of September 1, 2022 and $ 1.99 billion as of September 2, 2021. ... Depreciation expense was $ 7.03 billion, $ 6.13 billion, and $ 5.57 billion for 2022, 2021, and 2020, respectively.
risk_signals.page_location: Notes - Property, Plant, and Equipment (HTML lines 2870-2871)
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: The equipment base grew 18.2% YoY ($51,902M -> $61,354M gross) during the peak capex year, and $3.35B of equipment was not yet placed into service - a future depreciation step-up locked in just as the cycle turned down. Depreciation of $7.03B is the single largest cost assumption in the P&L; each 1-year error in average equipment life is worth roughly $1B+ of annual expense.
evidence_chain: Equipment gross +18.2% YoY to $61,354M; total PP&E gross $81,331M; net PP&E $38,549M (line 2870)
$3.35B equipment not yet placed into service (+68% vs $1.99B in 2021) - capex ahead of the downturn
FY2022 depreciation $7.03B vs FY2021 $6.13B (+14.7%); accumulated depreciation $42,782M = 52.6% of gross PP&E
Newest, largest equipment cohort enters the 7-year schedule exactly as Q4 FY2022 demand collapses
Result: depreciation expense is locked to rise into the FY2023 trough regardless of utilization

risk_signals.source: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements - Lehi, Utah Fab and 3D XPoint
risk_signals.keyword_matched: loss of $ 23 million included in restructure and asset impairments ... charge of $ 435 million
risk_signals.text_excerpt: In the first quarter of 2022, we received $ 893 million from TI for the sale of the Lehi facility and disposed of $ 918 million of net assets, consisting primarily of property, plant, and equipment of $ 921 million ... As a result of the disposition of the Lehi facility and other related adjustments, we recognized a loss of $ 23 million included in restructure and asset impairments in the first quarter of 2022. In 2021, we recognized a charge of $ 435 million included in restructure and asset impairments in connection with the definitive agreement with TI ... to write down the assets held for sale to the expected consideration, net of estimated selling costs. ... We also recognized a charge of $ 49 million to cost of goods sold in 2021 to write down 3D XPoint inventory due to our decision to cease further development of this technology.
risk_signals.page_location: Notes - Lehi, Utah Fab and 3D XPoint (HTML lines 2778-2796); corroborated in Business Overview (lines 160-175)
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: The Lehi/3D XPoint exit is the filing's in-house proof that technology bets in memory can be stranded mid-life: a whole fab and technology platform abandoned, with $921M of PP&E sold at a loss and a $435M write-down recognized only when a sale agreement forced fair-value measurement - never through the depreciation schedule. FY2022's $23M loss is the closing entry of that cycle, demonstrating impairment recognition is episodic and transaction-triggered rather than schedule-driven.
evidence_chain: Q1 FY2022: Lehi fab sold to TI for $893M; $918M net assets (incl. $921M PP&E) disposed; $23M loss recognized (lines 2778-2784)
FY2021 precedent: $435M held-for-sale write-down + $49M 3D XPoint inventory write-down (lines 2784-2794)
A whole technology (3D XPoint) and fab were abandoned before end of depreciable life
Write-down recognized only upon sale agreement (Level 3 fair value), not via periodic depreciation revision
Result: technology-exit losses in memory materialize as sudden episodic charges; annual depreciation systematically fails to pre-provision them

risk_signals.source: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements - Restructure and Asset Impairments; Segment Information
risk_signals.text_excerpt: For the year ended 2022 2021 2020 Restructure and asset impairments $ 48 $ 488 $ 60 Restructure and asset impairments for 2022 and 2021 are primarily related to the sale of our Lehi, Utah facility. ... Restructure and asset impairments for 2020 primarily related to asset impairments and employee relocation and severance costs related to right-sizing our Lehi, Utah facility.
risk_signals.page_location: Notes - Restructure and Asset Impairments (HTML lines 3372-3376); income statement (line 2591)
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: FY2022's realized asset-impairment-class charge is only $48M (vs $488M in FY2021), and no new impairment program was initiated - consistent with a peak-cycle year. The three-year pattern ($60M -> $488M -> $48M, all Lehi-related) shows impairment at Micron clusters around discrete technology/facility exits, not around cycle conditions - so the FY2023 down-cycle write-downs were not pre-provisioned by any schedule change in FY2022.
evidence_chain: FY2022 restructure and asset impairments: $48M (vs $488M FY2021, $60M FY2020) - all three years Lehi-related
No new restructuring or impairment program in FY2022 (peak cycle)
Impairment history clusters around technology/facility exit events, not business cycle
Depreciation schedule unchanged across all three years despite the exit events
Result: small current-period impairment + direct historical record fits the D3=4 anchor (not 5, not 3)

risk_signals.source: MD&A - Critical Accounting Estimates - Goodwill; Notes - Segment and Other Information
risk_signals.keyword_matched: fair value for all of our reporting units substantially exceeded their carrying value
risk_signals.text_excerpt: Our qualitative assessment for the current year indicated that the fair value for all of our reporting units substantially exceeded their carrying value and that a quantitative assessment was unnecessary. ... As of September 1, 2022 and September 2, 2021, CNBU, MBU, SBU, and EBU had goodwill of $ 832 million, $ 198 million, $ 101 million, and $ 97 million, respectively.
risk_signals.page_location: Item 7. MD&A - Critical Accounting Estimates - Goodwill (HTML lines 2429-2432); Notes - Segment and Other Information (line 3454)
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: At the FY2022 peak, ALL reporting units passed the goodwill qualitative screen with substantial headroom - including SBU, whose entire $101M goodwill was impaired just one year later in FY2023. The swing from 'substantially exceeded' to full write-off within 12 months demonstrates how quickly memory-cycle cash-flow forecasts collapse - and that the 7-year PP&E depreciation schedule absorbed none of that swing in either year.
evidence_chain: FY2022 Q4 annual goodwill test: qualitative pass for all units, 'substantially exceeded' carrying value (lines 2429-2432)
SBU goodwill on the books at FY2022 end: $101M (line 3454)
Same unit's goodwill fully impaired in FY2023 on quantitative DCF test (per FY2023 10-K) - forecast collapse within 12 months
Goodwill test is forward-looking and still missed the downturn's severity at Q4 FY2022 testing date
Result: peak-year impairment tests provide no early warning; depreciation assumptions equally cycle-blind

risk_signals.source: MD&A - Critical Accounting Estimates - Property, Plant, and Equipment (impairment test)
risk_signals.keyword_matched: undiscounted expected future cash flows are less than the carrying value
risk_signals.text_excerpt: In cases where undiscounted expected future cash flows are less than the carrying value, an impairment loss is recognized equal to the amount by which the carrying value exceeds the estimated fair value of the assets. The estimate of future cash flows involves numerous assumptions which require significant judgment by us, including, but not limited to, future use of the assets for our operations versus sale or disposal of the assets, future selling prices for our products, and future production and sales volumes.
risk_signals.page_location: Item 7. MD&A - Critical Accounting Estimates (HTML lines 2512-2520)
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: The long-lived asset recoverability test compares carrying value to UNDISCOUNTED cash flows at the asset-group level - a very low bar for fabs that generate cash in almost any price environment. Identical policy wording to FY2023: the test structure shields the 7-year depreciation schedule from cyclical reality in both peak and trough years, explaining why FY2022 saw zero PP&E impairment and FY2023 would see inventory/goodwill write-downs with PP&E still untouched.
evidence_chain: Recoverability measured against undiscounted future cash flows - time value ignored (lines 2512-2515)
Assets pooled at group level, diluting obsolescence of any single tool generation
Key assumptions (future ASPs, volumes, use vs sale) are management-judgment-heavy
FY2022 outcome: zero PP&E impairment at peak; test design unchanged into the trough
Result: gap between 7-year accounting life and cyclical/technological reality can persist for years without income-statement recognition

risk_signals.source: MD&A - Results of Operations / Consolidated Gross Margin
risk_signals.keyword_matched: the memory and storage industry environment deteriorated sharply
risk_signals.text_excerpt: In the fourth quarter of 2022, the memory and storage industry environment deteriorated sharply due to global and macroeconomic challenges combined with downward inventory adjustments by customers, leading to significant reductions in bit shipments and average selling prices for both DRAM and NAND resulting in a 23% decline in revenue as compared to the third quarter of 2022. ... Our consolidated gross margin percentage declined to 39% in the fourth quarter of 2022 from 47% in the third quarter of 2022 ... To address our elevated inventory levels and reduce supply growth, in the first quarter of 2023, we are selectively reducing facility utilization in both DRAM and NAND.
risk_signals.page_location: Item 7. MD&A - Results of Operations (HTML lines 2102-2106); Consolidated Gross Margin (lines 2123-2129)
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: The cycle turned WITHIN the FY2022 reporting period: Q4 revenue -23% QoQ, gross margin 47%->39%, and management pre-announced selective utilization cuts for Q1 FY2023. Yet the FY2022 statements carry no underutilization cost, no inventory write-down, and no depreciation revision - the $7.03B depreciation charge reflects full-normal utilization assumptions while the assets' economic utilization was already falling at year-end.
evidence_chain: Q4 FY2022: industry 'deteriorated sharply'; bit shipments and ASPs down for both DRAM and NAND; revenue -23% QoQ (lines 2102-2106)
Gross margin 47% (Q3) -> 39% (Q4); further decline expected Q1 FY2023 (lines 2123-2127)
Q1 FY2023: selective facility utilization reductions in BOTH DRAM and NAND pre-announced (lines 2127-2129)
FY2022 recognized zero underutilization cost (vs $335M MTU in 2021, $382M fab underutilization coming in FY2023)
Result: time-based 7-year depreciation decouples from usage-based economic consumption the moment the cycle turns

risk_signals.source: MD&A - Liquidity and Capital Resources / Investing Activities
risk_signals.keyword_matched: $12.07 billion of expenditures for property, plant, and equipment
risk_signals.text_excerpt: For 2022, net cash used for investing activities consisted primarily of $12.07 billion of expenditures for property, plant, and equipment; inflows of $115 million of partner contributions for capital expenditures; $888 million of net inflows from the sale of the Lehi, Utah fab ... We estimate capital expenditures in 2023 for property, plant, and equipment, net of partner contributions, to be around $8 billion. ... As of September 1, 2022, we had purchase obligations of approximately $4.04 billion for the acquisition of property, plant, and equipment, of which approximately $2.97 billion is expected to be paid within one year.
risk_signals.page_location: Item 7. MD&A - Investing Activities (HTML lines 2342-2346); Liquidity (lines 2274-2279)
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: FY2022 capex of $12,067M equals 39.2% of revenue - the peak of a three-year capex supercycle ($8.2B -> $10.0B -> $12.1B) that maxed out capacity investment exactly at the cycle top. With $4.04B of equipment purchase obligations still outstanding at year-end and $3.35B of equipment not yet in service, the depreciation burden was pre-committed to rise into FY2023 even as revenue collapsed - capital intensity at Micron is structurally >25% in every year, peak or trough.
evidence_chain: FY2023 capex guided 'around $8 billion' - a 34% cut signaling management saw the downturn (lines 2274-2276)
$4.04B PP&E purchase obligations outstanding at year-end, $2.97B due within one year (lines 2277-2279)
$3.35B equipment not yet placed into service + $1,897M CIP = future depreciation locked in
Result: peak-year capex supercycle converts into fixed depreciation charges precisely when the revenue base shrinks

risk_signals.source: Item 1. Business - CNBU / Research and Development
risk_signals.text_excerpt: In 2022, we ramped our industry-leading 1α DRAM node. Our newest node, 1ß (1-beta), is on track to ramp manufacturing of CNBU products in 2023. ... Additionally, we began high volume manufacturing and sales of our HBM2E product. ... In DRAM, our 1α node was introduced several quarters ahead of the industry, and our newest node, 1ß, is on track to start ramping in manufacturing by the end of calendar 2022. We plan to implement EUV lithography on the DRAM node after 1ß. In NAND, the introduction of our 176-layer node was also ahead of the industry and we recently announced volume production of the worlds first 232-layer NAND.
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: FY2022 was an aggressive technology-transition year: 1-alpha DRAM ramp, 1-beta queued for 2023, EUV insertion planned on the post-1-beta node, world-first 232-layer NAND announced, and HBM2E high-volume manufacturing begun. Each transition requires new tool sets while prior-node equipment continues on 7-year schedules; EUV insertion in particular can devalue entire pre-EUV lithography tool fleets. The pace of disclosed transitions (5 DRAM nodes in production + 2 in pipeline) confirms the 1-2 year node cadence that anchors the D1 mismatch.
evidence_chain: 2022 production on 1x/1y/1z/1-alpha nodes; 1-alpha ramped in 2022; 1-beta ramp planned end of CY2022/2023 (lines 230-232, 638-640)
EUV lithography planned on the node after 1-beta - a capital-intensive discontinuity (lines 640-641)
World-first 232-layer NAND volume production announced; 176-layer ramped ahead of industry (lines 641-643)
HBM2E high-volume manufacturing began 2022 - entry into AI-driven HBM race (lines 237-238)
Result: competitive-technological refresh pressure continuously compresses economic life below the 7-year accounting life

risk_signals.source: Item 1A. Risk Factors - Manufacturing / Competition / Acquisitions
risk_signals.keyword_matched: underutilization of our production assets / excess and obsolescence charges / impairment ... technological advancements
risk_signals.text_excerpt: Many factors may result in a reduction of our output or a delay in ramping production, which could lead to underutilization of our production assets. ... A significant portion of our manufacturing costs are fixed and do not vary proportionally with changes in production output. ... Consequently, we may incur charges in connection with obsolete or excess inventories or we may not fully recover our costs, which would reduce our gross margins. ... which may result in excess and obsolescence charges in future periods. ... impairment of acquired intangible assets, goodwill, or other assets as a result of changing business conditions or technological advancements.
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: Risk Factors explicitly warn of production-asset underutilization, inventory obsolescence charges, and technology-driven impairment - all of which materialized in the very next fiscal year ($382M underutilization, $1.83B inventory write-down, $101M goodwill impairment in FY2023). Notably, Risk Factors contain NO signal of any depreciation useful-life change in FY2022 (verified by keyword search): the section corroborates impairment/obsolescence risk while treating the 7-year schedule as stable.
evidence_chain: Risk factor: output reductions 'could lead to underutilization of our production assets'; fixed manufacturing cost structure flagged (lines 970-979)
Risk factor: 'obsolete or excess inventories' and future 'excess and obsolescence charges' (lines 987-994)
Risk factor: impairment of goodwill/other assets from 'changing business conditions or technological advancements' (lines 1566-1568)
All three warnings realized in FY2023 - confirming these were live risks already at FY2022
No useful-life change disclosed anywhere in the filing (verified by keyword search)
Result: risk disclosure framework acknowledges technology/cycle-driven value loss but never connects it to the depreciation schedule

risk_signals.source: MD&A - Critical Accounting Estimates - Inventories; Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm (CAM)
risk_signals.keyword_matched: a 5% variance in the estimated selling prices would have changed the estimated net realizable value
risk_signals.text_excerpt: For example, a 5% variance in the estimated selling prices would have changed the estimated net realizable value of our inventory by approximately $337 million as of September 1, 2022. ... the Company had a net inventory balance for finished goods and work in process inventory totaling approximately $5.9 billion. As disclosed by management, determining the net realizable value of the Company's net inventories involves significant judgments, including projecting future average selling prices and future sales volumes.
risk_signals.page_location: Item 7. MD&A - Critical Accounting Estimates - Inventories (HTML lines 2491-2493); Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm - Critical Audit Matter (lines 3578-3590)
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: Even at the cycle peak, inventory NRV was PwC's Critical Audit Matter, with disclosed sensitivity of ~$337M per 5% ASP move and $5.9B of FG/WIP inventory exposed. FY2022 recorded no write-down, but ASPs fell far more than 5% in Q4 and after year-end - the same ASP assumptions underpin both inventory NRV and the cash-flow projections that justify 7-year equipment lives. The CAM's presence at the peak foreshadows the FY2023 $1.83B write-down.
evidence_chain: FY2022 CAM: NRV of finished goods and work in process inventories; FG+WIP balance ~$5.9B (lines 3578-3590)
Sensitivity: 5% ASP variance ≈ $337M NRV impact as of 2022-09-01 (lines 2491-2493)
Q4 FY2022 ASPs already declining 'significantly' for both DRAM and NAND (lines 2102-2106)
No NRV write-down recognized in FY2022 - estimate held at year-end despite deteriorating prices
Result: inventory is the leading edge of asset-value risk; the same ASP collapse later undermines equipment-life economics

annotation_methodology.source_document: Micron Technology, Inc. 2022 Annual Report on Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 1, 2022; filed/signed 2022-10-07)
annotation_methodology.text_extraction_method: HTML parsing with Python (regex tag-stripping, latin-1 decoding with errors replaced) + keyword search (useful life/lives, depreciation, impairment, obsolescence, write down/write-down, underutilization, prospectively, change in estimate, HBM, EUV, technology node, capital expenditures); every candidate hit manually verified in visible body text with line numbers; hidden ix:hidden XBRL tag matches excluded
annotation_methodology.cross_year_anchor_protocol: MU FY2023 confirmed annotation (D1=4/D2=3/D3=5/D4=5/D5=4, composite 4.20) used as the explicit anchor. Each dimension scored against the same anchor table; identical facts yield identical scores (D1/D2/D5), factual differences documented as the sole source of score deltas (D3: 5->4; D4: same tier 5). Disclosure-wording difference between years (equipment '5 to 7 years' FY2022 vs '7 years for production equipment' FY2023) investigated and determined to be disclosure refinement, not an estimate change - no score impact.
annotation_methodology.scoring_method: Five-dimension weighted scoring (D1 0.25 / D2 0.20 / D3 0.20 / D4 0.20 / D5 0.15), 1-5 integer scale per dimension, anchored to confirmed META 2023 benchmark (4.0), confirmed MU FY2023 (4.2), and draft GOOGL (4.25); manufacturing-asset (fab) basis applied for D1/D5 rather than cloud-server basis
annotation_methodology.human_verification: All quoted text excerpts and financial figures manually verified against original FY2022 10-K filing at cited HTML line numbers
annotation_methodology.limitation: Single-year 10-K analysis of a cyclical-peak year; ratios (capex/revenue 39.2%) reflect peak-year spending and are flagged as such. Micron does not disclose depreciation by asset class within the PP&E note (segment-level D&A disclosed at line 3454: total $7,116M). FY2022 inventory NRV write-down amount is not separately disclosed as zero - absence of any charge inferred from no quantified disclosure (only the $337M/5% sensitivity); FY2021 comparative figures ($335M MTU underutilization, $435M Lehi write-down) are prior-year context within the same filing.
